title: Inerrancy of Scripture
definition: The inerrancy of Scripture means that the Bible, in all that it teaches and affirms, is true and without error because God is truthful and does not lie.
summary: Because Scripture comes from God, it is trustworthy. Inerrancy does not ignore genre, figures of speech, ordinary language, quotation style, or historical setting. It means God's Word is truthful in what it intends to communicate.
christFocus: Jesus trusted Scripture completely. He appealed to its words, fulfilled its promises, and declared that Scripture cannot be broken. The truthfulness of Scripture points us to the truthful Savior.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: God cannot lie, and Scripture is God's Word. Therefore Scripture is true. Inerrancy protects the believer from treating the Bible as partly trustworthy and partly unreliable.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: If the Bible can be dismissed whenever it confronts human preference, then doctrine and discipleship lose their foundation. Trust in Scripture strengthens confidence in God's promises, commands, warnings, and Gospel.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: When Scripture challenges your thoughts, feelings, or assumptions, let God's Word correct you. The faithful response is not suspicion toward Scripture, but humble submission to the God who speaks truth.
